title: Joshua 5 — Circumcision at Gilgal and the captain of the host of YHWH before Yericho (Jericho)

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: Ketiv ʿbrnw 'we crossed' / Qere ʿoḇrām 'they crossed'; the line translates the Qere and the note records the ASV's Ketiv ('until we were passed over'). wəlōʾ-hāyâ ḇām ʿôḏ rûaḥ 'no more spirit in them' is the anthropological rûaḥ, correctly lower case. Gentilics follow the overlay '-ite' rule (founder point 2).
ʿăśê ləḵā ḥarḇôṯ ṣurîm wəšûḇ mōl ... šēnîṯ: 'knives of flint ... circumcise ... again, a second time' is exact. The LXX note on the knives buried with Joshua (LXX Josh 24:30-31a) is accurate.
wayyāmol ... ʾel-gibʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ: 'at the hill of the foreskins' (ASV); translating the descriptive toponym is defensible and recorded in the names entry.
wəzeh haddāḇār ʾăšer-māl: 'this is the reason why ... circumcised'; the apposition hazzəḵārîm kōl ʾanšê hammilḥāmâ is kept. Exact.
mulîm hāyû ... lōʾ-mālû: pluperfect 'had been circumcised' against 'they had not circumcised' (impersonal plural) is exact.
ʿaḏ-tōm kol-haggôy 'until all the nation ... were consumed'; lāṯeṯ lānû 'to give us' keeps the MT first person (ASV). Exact.
wəʾeṯ-bənêhem hēqîm taḥtām ʾōṯām māl yəhôšuaʿ: the fronted object 'them Yehoshua circumcised' mirrors the Hebrew. Exact.
kaʾăšer-tammû ... ləhimmôl ... ʿaḏ ḥăyôṯām: 'had finished being circumcised ... until they were healed' (ḥyh 'revive, recover'). Exact.
gallôṯî ... gilgāl: the gll wordplay is explained in the note without being forced into the line; the formula wayyiqrāʾ šēm hammāqôm is rendered 'the name ... was called' (impersonal). Defensible.
wayyaʿăśû ʾeṯ-happesaḥ bəʾarbāʿâ ʿāśār yôm laḥōḏeš bāʿereḇ bəʿarḇôṯ yərîḥô: exact.
mēʿăḇûr hāʾāreṣ mimmāḥŏraṯ happesaḥ maṣṣôṯ wəqālûy bəʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh: exact; ʿăḇûr 'produce' (hapax-like, BDB) is the standard rendering.
wayyišbōṯ hammān mimmāḥŏrāṯ: 'the manna ceased on the day after'; təḇûʾaṯ ʾereṣ kənaʿan 'the yield of the land of Kena'an'. Exact.
wəhinnēh-ʾîš ʿōmēḏ ləneḡdô wəḥarbô šəlûp̄â bəyāḏô ... hălānû ʾattâ ʾim-ləṣārênû: literal. The note correctly observes that vv 13-15 do not use malʾāḵ, so no identification is imported into the line.

citations: Boling and Wright, Joshua (AB 6; 1982), ad loc.
BDB s.v. ḥwh (Hishtaphel); HALOT s.v. ḥwh
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: wayyōʾmer lōʾ kî ʾănî śar-ṣəḇāʾ-YHWH ʿattâ ḇāʾṯî. MT lōʾ kept (LXX/Syr lô recorded); 'the captain of the host of YHWH' is the corpus rendering of śar haṣṣāḇāʾ. The changed 'bowed down' for wayyištāḥû is the neutral rendering: 'worshipped' would decide the figure is YHWH, 'made obeisance' would imply a human superior; the verb covers both and the narrative leaves the status open. ʾăḏōnî is the human address form. Reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 and stays out of the line.
šal-naʿalḵā mēʿal raḡleḵā: singular 'sandal' kept against the plural of Ex 3:5, and the note states the difference. Exact.

citations: genesis-woh / exodus-woh / 1-kings-woh gentilic practice (checked in the data)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Verified identical in all three overlays and identical in substance to the ratified Kings entry (long forms, tz, apostrophes, '-ite' gentilics, English chapter-title forms, which all nine titles carry). Every equivalence in the table was checked against the MT names in these chapters. Flagged only for founder point 2 (gentilics across the corpus, esp. 'the Pelishtite' beside central 'the Pelishtim'); the entry itself is philologically sound and claim_type direct is right for a presentation convention.

citations: Webb, The Book of Judges (NICOT; 2012), ad loc.
glossaryReview.reasoning: Inferred is correct, as for its Kings source: transliteration leaves the recognized ambiguity open, and Block and Webb support the reading of rûaḥ YHWH as the empowering force in Judges. The literal 'clothed' (Judg 6:34) is lexically exact (cf. 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20) and keeps Judges' four distinct verbs distinct. Founder point 4: recommend ship.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
glossaryReview.reasoning: Rule and inventory verified: the source marks exactly 15 Ketiv/Qere readings in 15 verses, and all 15 are translated as Qere with the Ketiv recorded; the three ASV-Ketiv sites (Josh 5:1; 6:7; Judg 13:17) are correctly identified. One factual fix: the Judg 6:5 Ketiv is written *yʾbw*; the consonants of יבאו are *ybʾw* (imperfect yāḇōʾû). Correct the entry in all three overlays and the JDG-WOH-6:5 note.

citations: Barthélemy, Gooding, Lust and Tov, The Story of David and Goliath (OBO 73; 1986)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Same rule as Kings; each listed versional reading was checked (Josh 5:14 LXX/Syr lô; 6:18 LXX 'covet'; 6:26 LXX plus; 10:13 LXX minus; 10:15, 43; Judg 6:7-10 4QJudgᵃ; 6:14 LXX; 13:19 LXX; 1 Sam 3:13 tiqqun; 5:4, 5:6, 6:19, 17:4, 17:12, 17:32, 17:52) and is accurately reported. The 1 Sam 6:18 exception is rightly carved out to its own entry.

citations: Boling and Wright, Joshua (AB 6; 1982), ad loc.
glossaryReview.reasoning: The rendering is right and direct: śar haṣṣāḇāʾ is the ordinary title, 'captain of the host' keeps the corpus ṣāḇāʾ link, and the identification debate is left open. One fix: the rationale cites '(Westermann; ...)' for the malʾaḵ-YHWH identification with no work or locator; Westermann wrote no Joshua commentary. Delete the name or give a locatable work.

Minor version is consistent with house practice. Correct one claim in the note: the parallel Torah diff also modifies hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship (wohChoice and rationale), so sequential application of two full-field replacements would drop one clause. See the hishtachavah op.

Content approved: the clause is append-only, matches the published Kings lines (1 Kgs 22:54; 2 Kgs 2:15; 17:35, 36 checked) and the neutral 'bowed down' at Josh 5:14. Revise only for the merge: the Torah diff replaces the same wohChoice and rationale from the same 2.83.0 base with its own 'bow down' clause. Apply one combined wohChoice (Yosef-cycle 'made obeisance' + Torah clause + Former Prophets clause) and both appended rationale paragraphs; the two clauses agree in substance.

citations: wave chapters and v2.83.0 base (scripted cross-check)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Scripted check: every central id cited in the nine chapters has its refId in the post-diff appliesTo; no op drops a v2.83.0 refId; each appliesToAdded equals the actual set difference; no FP refId is listed without a matching glossaryRef.

Additions limited to 'land' sites (13). The 10 removals of eretz where ʾereṣ/ʾarṣâ is 'ground' or 'earth' (Josh 5:14; Judg 6:37, 39, 40; 13:20; 1 Sam 3:19; 5:3, 4; 17:46, 49) and the removal of the Gen 25:34-specific va-yivez-esav citation at 1 Sam 17:42 are correct. Leftover: the JDG-WOH-6:37 note still cites `eretz`.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 15 lines. No line uses lens vocabulary. 5:13-15 render ʾîš, śar-ṣəḇāʾ-YHWH and wayyištāḥû in their ordinary senses ('a man', 'the captain of the host of YHWH', 'bowed down'), and no malʾāḵ is imported. The TBWTT ch. 3 'military adviser' reading is confined to the labelled reception note at 5:14, which quotes the canon accurately.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-1Sam-6:18-great-stone: Ship. ʾāḇēl cannot be construed (two failed agreements, contradiction with vv 14-15); ʾeḇen with LXX, Targum and some Hebrew MSS is the standard correction (Driver 1913; McCarter 1980). Ratify the exception exactly as narrowly worded (MT grammatically impossible + Hebrew-manuscript reading supported by the versions).
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-gentilics: Keep the Kings '-ite' rule in the Former Prophets now (option c); it maps one-to-one to the ASV and is already ratified for Kings. For the later corpus pass, the reviewer prefers (a) '-ite' throughout, with the central pelishtim-caphtor plural becoming 'the Pelishtites', because 'the Pelishtite' beside 'the Pelishtim' is the one jarring pair. No philological issue either way; it is a presentation choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-Judg-6:40-the-Elohim: Confirm. The ratified Kings text explicitly leaves the central narrative-subject rule ('the Elohim') in force and limits the article-less form to predicates, genitives and direct-speech subjects; the brief's paraphrase was inaccurate. Clause 6 applies the ratified text exactly.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-Judg-6:34-clothed: Ship. lāḇəšâ is literally 'clothed' (BDB; same idiom 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20; Block), and keeping Judges' four verbs distinct is a gain in accuracy.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-herem: Ship. 'devote(d) to destruction' is the standard modern rendering (NRSV; HALOT) and the only consistent one; it makes the Josh 6 / Josh 10 connection visible without moral editorializing.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-shofar-promotion: Approve the promotion after the refId fix (EXO-WOH-20:15 for 20:18; optionally add EXO-WOH-19:13). Retire the 1-kings-woh shofar entry to a pointer and let the exodus-woh overlays cite the central id.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן יָ֗מָּה וְכָל־מַלְכֵ֤י הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַיָּ֔ם אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֵ֧י הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן מִפְּנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־עברנו [עָבְרָ֑ם] וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבָ֗ם וְלֹא־הָ֨יָה בָ֥ם עוֹד֙ ר֔וּחַ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Emorites who were beyond the Yarden westward, and all the kings of the Kena'anites who were by the sea, heard that YHWH had dried up the waters of the Yarden before the children of Yisra'el until they had crossed over, that their heart melted, and there was no more spirit in them because of the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official:
*hāʾĕmōrî ... hakkənaʿănî* 'the Emorites ... the Kena'anites' (collective singular gentilics; ASV 'the Amorites ... the Canaanites') under the '-ite' rule of `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`. genesis-woh writes 'the Emori', 'the Kena'ani' (central `ten-nations-of-canaan`) and exodus-woh 'the Amorite', 'the Canaanite'; the difference is listed for the founder in the wave report. Yarden = Jordan; Yisra'el = Israel.

*ʿaḏ-ʿoḇrām* 'until they had crossed over' translates the Qere. The Ketiv *ʿbrnw* reads 'until we had crossed over', which the ASV follows ('until we were passed over'), perhaps as the voice of the generation that crossed (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). *wəlōʾ-hāyâ ḇām ʿôḏ rûaḥ* 'and there was no more spirit in them': the human *rûaḥ* as courage or vital energy, translated in lower case (cf. 1 Kgs 10:5); `ruach-yhwh-transliteration-former-prophets` reserves the transliteration for *rûaḥ YHWH*.

paragraphs.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ עֲשֵׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וְשׁ֛וּב מֹ֥ל אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁנִֽית׃

i18n.en: At that time YHWH said to Yehoshua, "Make for yourself knives of flint, and circumcise the children of Yisra'el again, a second time."

notes.official: *ḥarḇôṯ ṣurîm* 'knives of flint' (ASV): flint blades for circumcision, as with Tzipporah's *ṣōr* at Ex 4:25; the LXX adds at Josh 24:30 that these knives were buried with Yehoshua. *šûḇ mōl ... šēnîṯ* 'circumcise ... again, a second time' is explained in vv 4-7: the generation born in the wilderness was uncircumcised. Yehoshua = Joshua. Circumcision per central `brit-milah-circumcision-covenant`.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעַשׂ־ל֥וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וַיָּ֙מָל֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־גִּבְעַ֖ת הָעֲרָלֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua made himself knives of flint, and circumcised the children of Yisra'el at the hill of the foreskins.

notes.official: *gibʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ* 'the hill of the foreskins' (ASV) is translated, not transliterated ('Giv'at ha-Aralot'), because it is a descriptive designation that the narrative itself explains; Gilgal (v 9), explained only by a wordplay, stays a name (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַיֹּצֵא֩ מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם הַזְּכָרִ֜ים כֹּ֣ל ׀ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה מֵ֤תוּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And this is the reason why Yehoshua circumcised: all the people who came out of Mitzrayim, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Mitzrayim.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־מֻלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כָּל־הָעָ֖ם הַיֹּֽצְאִ֑ים וְכָל־הָ֠עָם הַיִּלֹּדִ֨ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֥ם מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם לֹא־מָֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: For all the people who came out had been circumcised; but all the people who were born in the wilderness on the way, as they came out of Mitzrayim, they had not circumcised.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י ׀ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה הָלְכ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ עַד־תֹּ֨ם כָּל־הַגּ֜וֹי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הַיֹּצְאִ֣ים מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֞י הַרְאוֹתָ֣ם אֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה לַֽאֲבוֹתָם֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔נוּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: For the children of Yisra'el walked forty years in the wilderness, until all the nation, the men of war who came out of Mitzrayim, were consumed, because they did not listen to the voice of YHWH; to whom YHWH swore that he would not let them see the land which YHWH swore to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

notes.official: *ʾăšer nišbaʿ YHWH laʾăḇôṯām lāṯeṯ lānû* 'which YHWH swore to their fathers to give us': the shift to the first person is in the Hebrew and is kept (ASV 'to give us'). Mitzrayim = Egypt. *ʾereṣ zāḇaṯ ḥālāḇ ûḏəḇāš* 'a land flowing with milk and honey' (Ex 3:8).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ הֵקִ֣ים תַּחְתָּ֔ם אֹתָ֖ם מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּי־עֲרֵלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כִּ֛י לֹא־מָ֥לוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And their sons, whom he raised up in their place, them Yehoshua circumcised; for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them on the way.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁר־תַּ֥מּוּ כָל־הַגּ֖וֹי לְהִמּ֑וֹל וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה עַ֥ד חֲיוֹתָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when all the nation had finished being circumcised, that they stayed in their places in the camp until they were healed.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֗וֹם גַּלּ֛וֹתִי אֶת־חֶרְפַּ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ גִּלְגָּ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Yehoshua, "This day I have rolled away the reproach of Mitzrayim from off you." And the name of that place was called Gilgal, unto this day.

notes.official: *gallôṯî ʾeṯ-ḥerpaṯ miṣrayim mēʿălêḵem* 'I have rolled away the reproach of Mitzrayim from off you': the verb *gll* 'roll' explains the name Gilgal by wordplay. The name itself probably means 'circle' (of stones, cf. 4:19-20) (Nelson, *Joshua*, OTL, 1997). The aetiological formulas follow `al-ken-qara-shemah-aetiological-naming-formula-cross-corpus` (here *wayyiqrāʾ šēm hammāqôm*) and `ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֡סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בָּעֶ֖רֶב בְּעַֽרְב֥וֹת יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el encamped in Gilgal; and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening, in the plains of Yericho.

notes.official: *wayyaʿăśû ʾeṯ-happesaḥ ... bəʿarḇôṯ yərîḥô* 'and they kept the Passover ... in the plains of Yericho' (Yericho = Jericho): the first Passover in the land, on the date of Ex 12:6 (the fourteenth day, at evening).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אכְל֜וּ מֵעֲב֥וּר הָאָ֛רֶץ מִמָּֽחֳרַ֥ת הַפֶּ֖סַח מַצּ֣וֹת וְקָל֑וּי בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And they ate of the produce of the land on the day after the Passover, unleavened cakes and parched grain, in the selfsame day.

notes.official: *mimmāḥŏraṯ happesaḥ* 'on the day after the Passover'; *maṣṣôṯ wəqālûy* 'unleavened cakes and parched grain'; *bəʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh* 'in the selfsame day' (`b-etzem-ha-yom-ha-ze-P-formula`). *mēʿăḇûr hāʾāreṣ* 'of the produce of the land' (`eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֨ת הַמָּ֜ן מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת בְּאָכְלָם֙ מֵעֲב֣וּר הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מָ֑ן וַיֹּאכְל֗וּ מִתְּבוּאַת֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽיא׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the manna ceased on the day after, when they ate of the produce of the land; and the children of Yisra'el had manna no more, but they ate of the yield of the land of Kena'an that year.

notes.official: *wayyišbōṯ hammān* 'And the manna ceased': the provision begun in Ex 16 ends when the people eat the produce of Kena'an, as Ex 16:35 anticipates (central `mannah-bread-from-heaven-ex-16-quranic-and-nt-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`). Kena'an = Canaan.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בִּירִיחוֹ֒ וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדּ֔וֹ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלוּפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ הֲלָ֥נוּ אַתָּ֖ה אִם־לְצָרֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Yehoshua was by Yericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man was standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. And Yehoshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us, or for our adversaries?"

notes.official: *wəhinnēh-ʾîš ʿōmēḏ ləneḡdô wəḥarbô šəlûp̄â bəyāḏô* 'and behold, a man was standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand': the figure is introduced as *ʾîš* 'a man', as the visitors of Gen 18:2 and the wrestler of Gen 32:25 are, and the drawn sword recalls the messenger who confronts Bil'am (Num 22:23, 31). The Hebrew of vv 13-15 does not use *malʾāḵ*. *hălānû ʾattâ ʾim-ləṣārênû* 'Are you for us, or for our adversaries?'

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ לֹ֗א כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י שַׂר־צְבָֽא־יְהוָ֖ה עַתָּ֣ה בָ֑אתִי וַיִּפֹּל֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ אֶל־פָּנָ֥יו אַ֙רְצָה֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֲדֹנִ֖י מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "No; but I am the captain of the host of YHWH; now I have come." And Yehoshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and said to him, "What does my lord say to his servant?"

notes.official:
*śar-ṣəḇāʾ-YHWH* 'the captain of the host of YHWH' (`sar-tzeva-yhwh-captain-of-the-host-of-yhwh-joshua-5`): *śar haṣṣāḇāʾ* is the ordinary title of an army commander (1 Sam 17:55 'the captain of the host'; 1 Kgs 1:19), and the construct with YHWH places the figure over YHWH's *ṣāḇāʾ*. That may be the heavenly host (1 Kgs 22:19, central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus`) or Israel's army as YHWH's (Ex 12:41 'all the hosts of YHWH'). ASV 'prince of the host of Jehovah'; NRSV, NJPS 'commander of the army of the LORD'. Whether the figure is the *malʾaḵ YHWH*, an angelic commander (cf. *śar* in Dan 10:13, 21) or a manifestation of YHWH is debated (Boling and Wright, *Joshua*, AB 6, 1982; Butler, *Joshua*, WBC 7, 1983).

*lōʾ kî ʾănî ...* 'No; but I am ...': the MT negative *lōʾ* refuses both alternatives of v 13. Some Hebrew manuscripts, the LXX and the Syriac read *lô* 'to him' ('and he said to him'), which the line does not adopt (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). *ʿattâ bāʾṯî* 'now I have come' is read as a separate clause, as in most modern versions; the ASV joins the two ('as captain ... am I now come'). Some commentators think the speech breaks off, since the commission it announces comes only at 6:2 (Nelson, *Joshua*).

*wayyištāḥû* 'and bowed down' (ASV 'did worship'), under the Former Prophets clause proposed for central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` (as 2 Kgs 2:15 'bowed down to him to the ground'). The verb covers both homage and worship, and the narrative does not say whom Yehoshua takes the figure to be. *meh ʾăḏōnî məḏabbēr* 'What does my lord say': *ʾăḏōnî* is the address to a superior, 'my lord', not the divine *ʾăḏōnāy*.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse as 'I am the captain of the host of Yahweh, I am now come!' and reads vv 13-15 as a contact between one of the creators, sent as a military adviser, and the Israelites before Yericho. The line renders the title and the verbs literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שַׂר־צְבָ֨א יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ שַׁל־נַֽעַלְךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔ךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֑וּא וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ כֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And the captain of the host of YHWH said to Yehoshua, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you are standing is holy." And Yehoshua did so.

notes.official: *šal-naʿalḵā mēʿal raḡleḵā kî hammāqôm ʾăšer ʾattâ ʿōmēḏ ʿālāyw qōḏeš hûʾ* 'Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you are standing is holy': the command repeats Ex 3:5, the burning bush, almost word for word, so that Yehoshua's encounter is modelled on Moshe's (Moshe = Moses). Joshua has the singular 'sandal' where Ex 3:5 has the plural. The figure gives no further commission in ch. 5.
